sections.html:
Owners in Perinton may hire an agent, sell on their own or accept cash. A cash quote is worth getting when the house needs repairs or the closing date is tight. The town has just finished a townwide revaluation, so every parcel carries a new assessment and buyers will read it closely.

Perinton lies in eastern Monroe County about 10 miles southeast of Rochester. Local paperwork runs through the Assessment Office and the Building and Codes Department, both at Town Hall on Turk Hill Road, and the Monroe County Clerk in Rochester records deeds.

The town covers 34.56 square miles and includes the Village of Fairport on the Erie Canal, plus hamlets such as Egypt and Bushnell's Basin. It had 47,479 people in 2020 and an estimated 46,823 on July 1, 2025. Owners occupy 79.2 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $310,200, median gross rent is $1,349, and median household income is $112,093 across 20,347 households.

About a quarter of residents are 65 or older, so many sales involve retirees who are relocating, shrinking their space or closing out an estate. For them a reliable closing day can matter more than squeezing out the top price.

Every assessment was redone because the last full update came in 2018 and its equalization rate had slid from 100 percent to 57 percent. A revaluation adds nothing to the total tax collected. It only redistributes the same levy among owners, and the new values first appear on the 2026 to 2027 tax bills.

The Assessment Office mailed 18,234 preliminary notices and completed 2,152 informal reviews. The Board of Assessment Review received 819 applications and scheduled 334 in-person hearings. Together the reductions from preliminary values came to $189,622,437, or 2.1 percent of the roll.

Before setting a price, set the new assessment beside actual closing prices of similar houses, especially if you bought or sold under the old values.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Perinton assessment?
sections.html:
Taxes cannot be grieved, but the assessment can. Grievance Day for the next cycle is Tuesday, May 25, 2027, and applications are accepted from May 1 until 8:00 p.m. that day. A mailed form must arrive by the deadline regardless of its postmark.

  • File New York form RP-524, with all four pages completed and signed.
  • Submit one original and five copies of the form with its supporting papers.
  • Back it with evidence such as a closing statement, listing history, comparable sales, an appraisal or building costs.
  • Rental or commercial property calls for income and expense figures covering at least three years.

You do not have to appear in person. Decisions are mailed on or before July 1. After that, the final roll sets the school tax bill for September 1, the town and county bill for January 1 and any village bill for June 1.

The assessment cycle gives a rough timeline. The Assessment Office inspects new construction, remodeling and demolitions from July 1 through March 1, and informal reviews open each October 1. The tentative roll is filed May 1 and the final roll July 1, so a sale in late spring happens while next year's number is still being argued.

Perinton assessment cycle
DateStep
October 1Informal reviews open
March 1Inspections for new work end and exemption applications are due
May 1Tentative roll filed and grievance applications open
July 1Final roll filed and Board decisions mailed by this date

Read your preliminary assessment notice and check it against recent sales on the town's sales file. Make sure each deck, finished basement or addition has a closed permit. Find out if the house is in Fairport village, where a village bill may apply. With the deed, payoff statements and exemption paperwork in hand, you can judge an agent sale, a private sale and a cash offer side by side.

Apply by March 1 for exemptions the town runs. The Assessment Office covers these:

  • Senior Citizen.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income.
  • Veteran exemptions.
  • Volunteer Firefighter or Volunteer Ambulance Worker.
  • STAR, which the State administers at tax.ny.gov/star or (518) 457-2036.

Seniors who already hold an exemption are mailed a renewal, and each renewal sets an intake appointment. Call the Assessment Office at (585) 223-0770 with questions. The buyer files after closing.

sections.h2: Building and Codes and your sale
sections.html:
Skipping a required permit can hold up a sale and may complicate an insurance claim. The town can also issue stop work or cease and desist orders until a permit is obtained. Permits are needed for decks, porches, three-season rooms, finished basements, garages, sheds, fireplaces, generators, fences, hot tubs and pools that hold 24 inches of water or more.

Re-roofing, re-siding, flooring, cabinet installation and replacing windows or doors without enlarging openings usually do not need one. A final inspection leads to a Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy, and the space cannot be used until one is issued. A home business needs both a building permit and a Certificate of Occupancy before it starts. Ask the Building and Codes Department for your address history before listing.

sections.h2: What to bring and what a cash sale skips
sections.html:
Pull together a folder before you call buyers: the deed, your latest school and town and county tax bills, proof of any exemption, permit records with the Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy for decks and finished basements, and payoff statements for any mortgage or lien. With it you can compare offers quickly.

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal or loan approval, so the timeline depends on title work, the payoff and recording with the Monroe County Clerk. Ask for the offer in writing, find out who pays each closing cost, and have an attorney read the contract. If you hold an exemption, tell the buyer that it ends with the sale and the new owner files for their own.

The Monroe County Sheriff provides primary law enforcement, and the Village of Fairport has its own police department. Four volunteer fire protection districts split the town: Bushnell's Basin, Egypt, Forest Hills and Perinton. A house inside the village can also carry a village tax bill, so ask where the parcel sits.

Delinquent taxes lead to Monroe County's in rem foreclosure, so clear any balance before you sell. Recording a deed at the county costs $50 for the first page, and the state taxes the transfer at $2 per $500.

faqs.q: Did Perinton reassess every home recently?
faqs.a: Yes. The town completed a townwide revaluation in 2026, the first since 2018. The Assessment Office mailed 18,234 preliminary notices, and the new values appear on the 2026 to 2027 tax bills.

faqs.q: When is the next Perinton Grievance Day?
faqs.a: May 25, 2027, with filing open from May 1 and a final deadline of 8:00 p.m. that evening. Late or postmark-only mailings will not be reviewed.

faqs.q: Does a revaluation raise my taxes?
faqs.a: Not by itself. The town's tax levy is set through budgets, so a new assessment only changes how that total is shared. Your bill can rise, fall or stay level depending on how your value compares with others.

faqs.q: Is Fairport the same as Perinton?
faqs.a: No. The Village of Fairport is one part of the town of Perinton, located on the Erie Canal. A village tax bill may apply to parcels inside the village.

faqs.q: Can unpermitted work stop a Perinton sale?
faqs.a: It can. Work done without a required permit may hold up a sale and complicate insurance claims, and a space cannot be occupied until the Building and Codes Department issues a Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy.
